sentences.text: Case diary is perused.
Learned counsel for the rival parties are heard.

Both the aforesaid cases relate to the same crime
number against both the petitioners who are partners in business and therefore have been heard
analogously and are being decided by the present common order.
These are 1st applications u/S.438 Cr.P.C. filed by the petitioners for grant of anticipatory bail.
Petitioners

apprehend arrest in connection with offences punishable u/Ss.270, 272, 273, 420 of Ipc
r/w 57, 59, 63 and 64 of Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006 registered as Crime No.1132/2018 at
Police Station City Kotwali Morena.

Learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the applications and prayed for its rejection by
contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant
of anticipatory bail is made out.

The allegation against both the petitioners is that they were found manufacturing the spurious
paneer with the help of synthetic material such as caustic soda and certain chemicals with milk as
not one of the ingredients.

The prosecution has alleged offence of cheating punishable u/S.420 o Ipc along with the aforesaid
offence probably with intent to render the offences non-bailable.

Pertinently, all other offences
except Sec.420 of Ipc alleged against petitioners are bailable as punishment provided for the same
are not more than 3 months.

sentences.text:
This Court was initially of the prima facie view that the offence of cheating does not appear to be
attracted as the definition of cheating u/S.415 of Ipc essentially requires as a per-requisites that
there should be a person indulging in cheating and another who is cheated.

In the incident,
allegation discloses that mere manufacturing of spurious paneer is alleged with no allegation of any
other person having been deceived to part with his property by purchase of spurious paneer.
After hearing learned counsel for the State, Smt. Ami Prabal, Deputy Advocate General who has
opposed the grant of anticipatory bail by raising the plea of larger public interest, this Court deems it
appropriate to indulge in a deeper probe to ascertain the involvement of the element of cheating or
not.

To ascertain as to whether the offence of cheating punishable u/S. 420 Ipc is made out or not, it
would be appropriate to closely scan the definition of cheating in Sec. 415 Ipc which is reproduced
below:-
Sec. 415. Cheating.--Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the
person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain
any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he
would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to
cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to "cheat".
Explanation.--A dishonest concealment of facts is a deception within the meaning of this section.
Cheating is constituted when deceit is exercised by any person in a fraudulent or dishonest manner
resulting in inducing another who is deceived to deliver any property to any person or to consent
that any person shall retain any property or intentionally induces a person so deceived to do or omit
to do anything which he would not do or omit if he was not so deceived.
The definition culminates with the stipulation that such act or omission on the part of the person
deceived either causes or is likely to cause harm in mind, reputation or property to the person
deceived.
Explanation to Sec. 415 Ipc further clarifies that dishonest concealment of facts is a deception
within the meaning of cheating.
In the instant case, the Fir dated 20/10/2018 is lodge based on the complaint of the complainant
who is a Food Safety Officer of District Morena which is founded on the revelation made on raid
carried out by Tehsildar on the request of the Food Safety Officer at the firm-Sai Baba Milk Dairy
Product situated in an industrial area of District Morena.

In the said raid 800 kg of paneer kept in
the premises of the said fi
rm in thermocol packing was found.

sentences.text: 2 vanaspati, skimmed milk powder and caustic soda were found in the premises of the said firm where the directors were the petitioners herein.
Samples were obtained by the raiding team of the said raw materials and send for chemical analysis to the FSL.
The entire raw materials were seized and sealed.
It was found that the said two directors of the firm were manufacturing artificial paneer and used to sell it outside district Morena.
The FIR further discloses that the petitioners had indulged in similar offences registered in 2017.

When the factual matrix is tested on the anvil of the definition of cheating it appears that the petitioners are alleged to have indulged in manufacturing artificial paneer and by transporting the same outside the district are alleged to have soled the same in open market which has been consumed by large number of people under the impression that the same is pure made from milk.
The transporters and consumers have been deceived into transporting and consuming the said artificial panner which they have would not have done they known about the paneer being artificial.
Therefore, it is evident that the petitioners have indulged in deceiving the consumers into consuming the artificial paneer by dishonest concealment of the fact of paneer being artificial.
In the considered opinion of this court, a prima facie case of cheating is made out.
More so, the petitioners have indulged in an act which must have caused harm to the health member of the public.
The element of deceit exercised is palpable on the face of record, and therefore this court especially in view of the investigation being pending declines grant of anticipatory bail.
The interim anticipatory bail order passed by this Court on 30.11.2018 shall stand withdrawn.
Accordingly, both the petitions stand rejected.

(Sheel Nagu) Judge 13.12.2018 SS SATEESH KUMAR SEN 2018.12.21 14:55:39 -08'00'
